strings.d1.s0.name: Tegallalang Rice Terrace
strings.d1.s0.tips: Terraced rice fields, quiet and cool at 07:30. The swing is optional, 150,000 IDR.
strings.d1.s1.name: Tirta Empul
strings.d1.s1.tips: A holy spring purification temple. Sarongs are provided, and the pool has 13 fountains.
strings.d1.s2.name: Ubud Palace
strings.d1.s2.tips: The royal palace courtyard, with an evening legong dance (100,000 IDR).
strings.d1.s3.name: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka
strings.d1.s3.tips: The roast pork Bourdain praised, opposite the palace. It sells out by lunchtime.
strings.d1.s4.name: Ubud Monkey Forest
strings.d1.s4.tips: A sacred monkey forest with temples. Watch your glasses and bag.
strings.d1.b0.name: Warung Babi Guling Gung Cung
strings.d1.b0.tips: Local babi guling (roast suckling pig) near the palace.
strings.d1.b1.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk
strings.d1.b1.tips: A 2 km ridge walk, also good for sunset.
strings.d2.s0.name: Mount Batur Sunrise Trek
strings.d2.s0.tips: You are picked up from your hotel at 02:00. Climb for 2 hours, then watch sunrise at 1,717 m and eat eggs cooked in volcanic steam. Tour ~450,000 IDR.
strings.d2.s1.name: Toya Devasya Hot Springs
strings.d2.s1.tips: Hot springs on the shore of Lake Batur, welcome after the trek.
strings.d2.s2.name: Ubud Art Market
strings.d2.s2.tips: A souvenir market. Start bargaining at half the asking price.
strings.d2.s3.name: Warung Biah Biah Ubud
strings.d2.s3.tips: Balinese tapas (small plates), local and affordable.
strings.d2.s4.name: Saraswati Temple
strings.d2.s4.tips: A temple with a lotus pond, next to Starbucks.
strings.d2.b0.name: Warung Pulau Kelapa Ubud
strings.d2.b1.name: Tegenungan Waterfall
strings.d2.b1.tips: A waterfall close to Ubud, an alternative to the hot springs.
strings.d3.theme: Ubud to Canggu via Tanah Lot
strings.d3.s0.name: Jatiluwih Rice Terraces
strings.d3.s0.tips: UNESCO-listed terraces, wider and calmer than Tegallalang, with walking trails.
strings.d3.s1.name: Ulun Danu Beratan Temple
strings.d3.s1.tips: A temple that appears to float on the lake, with misty mountains behind.
strings.d3.s2.name: Jatiluwih Warung Dhea
strings.d3.s2.tips: Nasi campur (mixed rice plate) with a terrace view.
strings.d3.s3.name: Tanah Lot
strings.d3.s3.tips: A rock temple in the sea. Sunset is the famous moment, and it gets crowded.
strings.d3.s4.name: Canggu Batu Bolong Beach
strings.d3.s4.tips: Canggu's beach bars: beer and surf lights after sunset.
strings.d3.b0.name: Old Man's Canggu
strings.d3.b0.tips: A beach bar, best in the evening.
strings.d3.b1.name: Handara Gate
strings.d3.b1.tips: The Instagram gate, next to the lake temple.
strings.d4.s0.name: Echo Beach Canggu
strings.d4.s0.tips: A surf lesson (~350,000 IDR) or a morning swim. The waves are clean in the dry season.
strings.d4.s1.name: Crate Cafe Canggu
strings.d4.s1.tips: Canggu's brunch culture, with smoothie bowls.
strings.d4.s2.name: Seminyak Village
strings.d4.s2.tips: Boutiques and a mall on Oberoi Street.
strings.d4.s3.name: Babi Guling Pak Malen Seminyak
strings.d4.s3.tips: Seminyak's babi guling (roast suckling pig), with crispy skin.
strings.d4.s4.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset
strings.d4.s4.tips: Ku De Ta or Potato Head beach club (minimum spend), or a beanbag on the sand for sunset.
strings.d4.b0.name: Potato Head Beach Club
strings.d4.b0.tips: A beach club with a pool and DJ.
strings.d4.b1.name: Petitenget Temple
strings.d4.b1.tips: Seminyak's temple, best on ceremony days.
strings.d5.s0.name: Kelingking Beach
strings.d5.s0.tips: 45 minutes by speedboat from Sanur, plus a tour by vehicle (~900,000 IDR). See T-Rex Rock and the view from the top (the descent takes 1 hour and is difficult).
strings.d5.s1.name: Angel's Billabong
strings.d5.s1.tips: A natural pool. Swimming is forbidden at high tide.
strings.d5.s2.name: Broken Beach
strings.d5.s2.tips: A cove with a natural rock arch.
strings.d5.s3.name: Nusa Penida Warung Crystal Bay
strings.d5.s3.tips: A warung at Crystal Bay serving nasi goreng (fried rice).
strings.d5.s4.name: Crystal Bay Snorkelling
strings.d5.s4.tips: See manta rays at Manta Point (boat ~200,000 IDR) or snorkel at Crystal Bay. The boat leaves at 16:00.
strings.d5.b0.name: Diamond Beach
strings.d5.b0.tips: White sand in east Penida, instead of snorkelling.
strings.d5.b1.name: Penida Colada Beach Bar
strings.d6.s0.name: Padang Padang Beach
strings.d6.s0.tips: A small cove reached through the rocks. Quiet in the morning, with monkeys around.
strings.d6.s1.name: Bingin Beach Warung
strings.d6.s1.tips: Grilled fish at the cliffside warungs, reached by stairs.
strings.d6.s2.name: Single Fin Uluwatu
strings.d6.s2.tips: A cliff bar: watch the surf and have lunch.
strings.d6.s3.name: Uluwatu Temple
strings.d6.s3.tips: A sea temple on the cliff. Monkeys snatch glasses, and a sarong is included in the entry fee.
strings.d6.s4.name: Kecak Fire Dance Uluwatu
strings.d6.s4.tips: A kecak dance with 100 performers at sunset. Buy your ticket at 17:00 and sit near the front.
strings.d6.b0.name: Suluban Beach
strings.d6.b0.tips: A surf beach reached through a cave, instead of Padang Padang.
strings.d6.b1.name: Jimbaran Bay Seafood Grill
strings.d6.b1.tips: Grilled seafood on the sand, on the way back from Uluwatu.
strings.d7.s0.name: Sanur Beach Promenade
strings.d7.s0.tips: A 5 km seafront path, with sunrise on Bali's east coast and calm water.
strings.d7.s1.name: Sindhu Market Sanur
strings.d7.s1.tips: A morning market for bubur (rice porridge) and coffee.
strings.d7.s2.name: Sanur Village Spa
strings.d7.s2.tips: A Balinese massage to say goodbye.
strings.d7.s3.name: Warung Mak Beng Sanur
strings.d7.s3.tips: Fried fish and soup since 1941, with a single set menu.
strings.d7.s4.name: Ngurah Rai Airport Transfer
strings.d7.b0.name: Genius Cafe Sanur
strings.d7.b0.tips: A beachfront cafe for a light bite.
strings.d7.b1.name: Le Mayeur Museum Sanur
strings.d7.b1.tips: The home of the Belgian painter, instead of the spa.
strings.note0: Bali has no public transport: use a scooter (international licence and helmet), Grab/Gojek or a car with a driver by the day (~700,000 IDR). Allow 1-2 hours of traffic between Ubud, Canggu and Uluwatu.
strings.note1: April to October is the dry season, ideal for surfing, Batur and Penida. July and August are crowded and expensive.
strings.note2: Sarongs and sashes are compulsory at temples (provided at the entrance). Do not enter during menstruation, and be respectful on ceremony days.
strings.note3: Babi guling costs 40-60,000 IDR at a warung and nasi campur 30-50,000. Beach club minimum spend is 300-500,000.
strings.note4: Monkeys (Uluwatu, Monkey Forest) snatch glasses and phones. Do not show them food.
strings.note5: Take the morning boat from Sanur for the Nusa Penida tour. The Kelingking descent is difficult, so looking from above is enough.
